חוֹמֶשׁ m. (Biblical Hebrew חֹמֶשׁ; חמש)
1) one fifth, especially one fifth of the value to be added as fine on restoring misappropriated property or redeeming dedicated property (Vayikra V, 16; 24; XXVII, 27). Bava Kamma IX, 6. Bava Metzia 54ᵃ חוֹמְשׁוֹ של קרן the fifth part of the principal (assessed value), i.e. one plus one fifth, see next word; and from

—2) Ḥomesh, one of the five books of Moses, also one of the five books of Psalms. Sotah 36ᵇ ח׳ הפיקודים the Book of Numbers; ח׳ שני the Book of Exodus; and from—plural חוֹמָשִׁים, חוֹמָשִׁין. Bava Metzia VI, 8 חמשה ח׳ הן there are five things to which the law ordaining the addition of one fifth applies.—Chagigah 14ᵃ חמשה חוֹמְשֵׁי תורה the five books of the Law. Yerushalmi Megillah III, 74ᵃ top ח׳ single parts of the Pentateuch. Kiddushin 33ᵃ שני ח׳ two books of the Psalms.

נָשָׂא (Biblical Hebrew; compare נָסָה)
1) to lift up, carry. Sotah 35ᵃ נ׳ ארון את נוֹשְׂאָיו the Ark carried its carriers. Pirkei Avot Chaldaic VI נוֹשֵׂא בעול וכ׳ helps his brother to bear his yoke. Berakhot III, 1 נוֹשְׂאֵי המטה, see מִטָּה. Megillah 9ᵃ (one of the changes in translating the Bible into Greek) נוֹשֵׂא בני אדם a carrier of men (for חֲמֹר, Shemot IV, 20); and see from—Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 6 אני מרומם ונושא את ראשם I will raise and elevate their head; see infra.—נ׳ כפים, see כַּף.—נ׳ פנים to lift up the face, to respect, favor, spare, be partial. Chagigah 14ᵃ (explained נשוא פנים, Isaiah III, 3) זה שנוֹשְׂאִין פ׳ לדורו בעבורו he for whose sake his generation is favored in heaven. Shabbat 13ᵇ שלא נ׳ פ׳ לתורה who spared him not for the sake of his scholarship. Yoma 87ᵃ שנָשְׂאוּ לו פ׳ בעה"ז that indulgence was shown him (by the Lord) in this world. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 11 לא אֶשָּׂא פ׳ מפניך shall I not favor thee for thy own sake? Ib. כשם שהם נוֹשְׂאִין לי וכ׳ as they (the Israelites) honor me (by saying grace even after a scanty meal), so do I favor them; and from—נ׳ נפש אל to lift up the soul to, to long for. Midrash Till. to Psalms XXV, 1 למה אתה נושא נפשך אלי why dost thou lift up thy soul to me (why dost thou depend on me)?; Yalkut ib. 701.—נ׳ קרבן to offer up a sacrifice. Ib. 702 אדם חוטא ונושא ק׳ if a man sinned, he offered &c.; Midrash Till. l. common gender. נושא ומביא ק׳ (correct accordingly)—Part. pass. נָשׂוּא, f. נְשׂוּאָה &c. Ib. עכשו … הרי נפשנו נ׳ לך now that we have no sacrifices, our soul is lifted up to thee.

—2) to lift, remove. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. l. common gender. (reference. to the double meaning of נ׳, to raise and to remove) לכו שְׂאוּ את ראשו go and remove (or lift up) his head; and from—נ׳ עון to forgive. Yerushalmi Sanhedrin X, beginning, 27ᶜ (reference. to Shemot XXXIV, 7) נושא עוונות אין וכ׳ the text does not say, ‘removing iniquities’, but ‘removing iniquity’, the Lord takes away (from the scales) one bond of man’s sins, and the merits prevail &c.; Yerushalmi Peah I, 16ᵇ bottom of page (correct accordingly); Yalkut Shemot 400; see שְׁטַר. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 45; and e.

—3) to take, especially נ׳ ונתן to take and give, to deal; to transact, argue. Shabbat 31ᵃ נָשָׂאתָ ונתת באמונה hast thou (while on earth) been dealing honestly? Bava Metzia 48ᵃ הנושא ונותן בדברים he who concludes a bargain verbally. Midrash Tanḥuma Sh’moth 18 כשם שנושאין ונותנין בהלכה וכ׳ as well as they debate on the law below, so do they above. Ib. שנושאין ונותנין בדין וכ׳ they argue in court, and the Lord argues with them; and from

—4) נ׳ אשה, or נ׳ to take a wife into one’s house, to marry. Ketubot II, 1 בתולה נְשָׂאתַנִי thou hast married me as a virgin; אלמנה נְשָׂאתִיךְ I married thee as a widow. Yevamot 37ᵇ לא יִשָּׂא אדם וכ׳ one may not marry in one country and go away &c. Moʿed Katan I, 7 אין נושאין נשים וכ׳ no marriages may take place during the festive week; and see from—Part. pass. נָשׂוּי (followed by accus.) having married; f. נְשׂוּאָה (followed by ל) being married to; plural נְשׂוּאִים, … אִין; נְשׂוּאוֹת. Yevamot III, 6 ואחד נ׳ נכרית one of them has married a stranger. Ib. ומתו הנ׳ את האחיות and those brothers who had married two sisters died. Ib. I, 2 (2ᵇ) היתה … נשואה לאחיו Yerushalmi ed. (Mishnah ed. נשואת, correct accordingly; Bavli ed. נשואות) if his daughter or … was married to &c.; and from—Tosefta ib. VI, 5 נָשׂאוּי.

Nifal - נִישָּׂא
1) to be lifted up, removed &c. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. l. common gender. כבר … שיִנָּשְׂאוּ את ראשם וכ׳ it had been decreed that their head should be lifted (see supra): turn its meaning and elevate their head.

—2) f. נִישֵּׂאת, נִשֵּׂ׳, נִישֵּׂת, נִיסֵּת to be married. Ketubot I, 1 בתולה נ׳ וכ׳ a virgin’s marriage takes place on the fourth day of the week. Ib. V, 2 הגיע … ולא נִשְּׂאוּ if the time set for marriage expired and they were not taken in marriage. Yevamot II, 10 מותרות לִינָּשֵׂא להם they may marry them. Ib. 88ᵇ הרי זו לא תִנָּשֵׂא ואם ניסת וכ׳ she must not marry again, and if she does &c.; Ketubot 22ᵇ; and see from

Hifil - הִשִּׂיא
1) to lift up, to announce by signals (the New Moon). Rosh Hashanah II, 2, and e. מַשִּׂיאִין, see מַשּׂוּאָה. Yerushalmi ib. II, 58ᵃ top אין משיאין לילי זמנו we do not raise signals in the night of the regular New Moon (from the 29ᵗʰ to the 30ᵗʰ) &c.; and from—Tosefta ib. II (I), 2 מַסִּיעִין את החדש ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (משיא׳ על, מסיא׳) we signalize the New Moon.

—2) to transfer. Devarim Rabbah section (Parashah) 11 (reference. to ישא, Psalms IXXV, 5) יַשִּׂיא ברכה לאחרים he will bring blessing upon others.

—3) to move, remove, pass. Beitzah III, 7 מַשִּׂיאָהּ על גבי חברתה he may pass one knife over the other (to whet it). Tosefta Parah X (IX), 3 הִשִּׂיאוֹ לדבר אחר he diverted his mind towards another subject; Pirkei Avot Zar. II, 5. Yerushalmi ib. II, 41ᶜ bottom of page היה לו להַשִּׂיאוֹ וכ׳, see הֶשֵּׂיאָה.

—4) to transfer, transcribe, translate. Tosefta Sotah VIII, 6 הִשִּׂיאוּ את הכתב וכ׳ they transcribed the inscription on the stones in seventy languages; Sotah 35ᵇ; Yerushalmi ib. VII, 21ᵈ bottom of page

—5) to give away in marriage; to cause to marry. Ketubot 111ᵇ כל המַשִּׂיא בתו וכ׳ he who marries his daughter to a scholar. Ib. 67ᵇ top מַשִּׂיאִין את היתומה וכ׳ we must first help the fatherless maiden to marry, and then the fatherless lad. Kiddushin 29ᵃ האב חייב … ולהַשִּׂיאוֹ אשה a father is bound to …, and to provide a wife for him; and from

Hithpaël - הִתְנַשֵּׂא to be raised; to exalt one’s self, to boast. Pirkei Avot Zar. 44ᵃ, see הָלַם. Berakhot 63ᵇ להִתְנַשֵּׂא, see נָבַל; and e.

comments.he: כדרבי אבהו - להעמיד לפניו מתורגמן לדרוש ברבים:
למעלה נושאין פנים בעבורו לדורו - שהכל ניזונין בזכותו כגון רבי חנינא בן דוסא כדאמרינן בעלמא (תענית דף כד:): כל העולם אינו ניזון אלא בשביל חנינא בני:
למטה - מלכי האומות מכבדין אותן בשבילו כגון ר' אבהו שהיה חשוב בבית המלך כדאמרינן במסכת סנהדרין (דף יד.): דהוו נפקי אמהתא דבי קיסר לאפיה כו':

"שר חמשים" — אל תקרי [תקרא] "שר חמשים" אלא "שר חומשין" — זה שיודע לישא וליתן בחמשה חומשי תורה. דבר אחר: "שר חמשים" יש להבינו כפי שאמר ר' אבהו, שאמר ר' אבהו: מכאן שאין מעמידין מתורגמן על הצבור (שיתרגם להם דברי תורה או דברי החכמים) מי שהוא פחות מחמשים שנה. "ונשוא פנים" — זה שנושאין פנים לדורו בעבורו. ויש בכך אופנים שונים: יש שנושאים לו פנים למעלה בעולם עליון, כגון ר' חנינא בן דוסא שהתפלל על הדור ונענה בתפילותיו, ויש למטה, כגון ר' אבהו שהיו נושאים פנים לישראל בגללו בי [בבית] הקיסר.

comments.en: A tanna who lived at the end of the Second Temple period, Rabbi Ĥanina ben Dosa was a disciple of Rabban Yoĥanan ben Zakkai. However, he is best known as the performer of miraculous acts, a righteous man whose prayers were always heard on high. The Talmud is replete with stories of miracles that took place for him and for those close to him. He was indigent and earned a very meager living. He is the Talmud’s paradigm of a full-fledged righteous man who received no reward in this world. In tractate Avot, several of his ethical teachings are cited. They underscore the primacy of the fear of Heaven and the need for mutual affection in interpersonal relationships.

Aĥer can be understood literally as: A different person, one who was unknown beforehand. However, the word apparently included a negative connotation as well, similar to the use of the term Aĥerim, literally, others, in rabbinic literature as a reference to gentiles. It is also possible that it is related to the verb aĥar, which means: In heat, enslaved to his lusts.

comments.he: רבי חנינא בן דוסא למעלה - שהיה בעל מעשים יותר מכל בני דורו:
ולמטה בבית קיסר - ולאו משום שלא היה חשוב למעלה אלא משום שגם בדורו היו אנשי מעשה כמותו:

sections.en: “A captain of fifty,” do not read it as “sar ḥamishim,” rather read it as “sar ḥumashin”; this is one who knows how to engage in discourse with regard to the five books of [ḥamisha ḥumshei] the Torah. Alternatively, “a captain of fifty” should be understood in accordance with Rabbi Abbahu, for Rabbi Abbahu said: From here we learn that one may not appoint a disseminator over the public to transmit words of Torah or teachings of the Sages if he is less than fifty years of age. “And the man of favor”; this is one for whose sake favor is shown to his generation. The Gemara provides different examples of this: Some garner favor above, such as Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa, whose prayers for his generation would invariably be answered. Others gain favor below, for example: Rabbi Abbahu, who would plead Israel’s case in the house of the emperor.
sections.he: ״שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁים״ — אַל תִּקְרֵי ״שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁים״, אֶלָּא ״שַׂר חוּמָּשִׁין״. זֶה שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לִישָּׂא וְלִיתֵּן בַּחֲמִשָּׁה חוּמְשֵׁי תוֹרָה. דָּבָר אַחֵר: ״שַׂר חֲמִשִּׁים״ — כִּדְרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: מִכָּאן שֶׁאֵין מַעֲמִידִין מְתוּרְגְּמָן עַל הַצִּבּוּר פָּחוֹת מֵחֲמִשִּׁים שָׁנָה. ״וּנְשׂוּא פָּנִים״ — זֶה שֶׁנּוֹשְׂאִין פָּנִים לְדוֹרוֹ בַּעֲבוּרוֹ. לְמַעְלָה, כְּגוֹן רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא. לְמַטָּה, כְּגוֹן רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ בֵּי קֵיסָר.

en: חֵרֵשׁ m. (Biblical Hebrew; compare חֲרַשׁ) [closed up,] deaf, dumb (compare אִלֵּם); deaf and dumb. Terumot I, 2 ח׳ שדברו וכ׳ the ḥeresh of which the scholars speak (in a legal sense) means everywhere deaf and dumb. Ib. ח׳ המדבר וכ׳ a ḥeresh that can talk but not hear. Megillah II, 4 חוץ מח׳ except a deaf person. Sifré Bamidbar 153 (reference. to Bamidbar XXX, 5; 12) להוציא את הח׳ this excludes the case of the father (the husband) being deaf; Nedarim 73ᵃ; and from—plural חֵרְשִׁים, חֵרְשִׁין. Chagigah 14ᵃ; Gittin 88ᵃ, see חָרָשׁ. Ruth Rabbah section (Parashah) 2 beginning (reference. to חרש, Joshua II, 1) עשו עצמכם ח׳ pretend to be deaf.—Fem. חֵרֶשֶׁת. Gittin V, 5. Yevamot XIV, 1; and e.—plural חֵרְשׁוֹת. Ib. 3.

חָכַם (Biblical Hebrew; see חָכָם)
1) to be wise, to know. Niddah 70ᵇ מה יעשה אדם ויֶחְכַּם what must one do in order to be wise?

—2) (denominative of חָכָם) to meet for deliberation. Ib. לכשיחיו נֶחְכַּם להן when they resurrect, we shall meet to discuss their case.

Hifil - הֶחְכִּים
1) to grow wise, to become a scholar. Bava Batra 25ᵇ הרוצה שיַחְכִּים he who desires to become a scholar; ib. 175ᵇ (Berakhot 63ᵇ שיִתְחַכֵּם). Pirkei Avot II, 5 … לא כל … מַחְכִּים not every one that has a large trade, becomes wise (experienced); and from

—2) to make wise, to stimulate a person’s mind by ingenious suggestions, questions &c. Chagigah 14ᵃ תלמיד המַחְכִּים וכ׳ a student who enlightens his teachers. Bava Metzia 107ᵇ ומַחְכִּימַת פתי and makes the simple wise.

—3) to subtilize, philosophize. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 6, beginning ה׳ על גזרתו וכ׳ philosophized on (tried to find out the reasons for) the Lord’s law. Ib. מה שהייתי מַחְכִּים וכ׳ when I philosophised … and made myself believe …, it was all vain boast &c.

Hithpaël - הִתְחַכֵּם,

Nithpaël - נִתְחַכֵּם to become wise. Berakhot 63ᵇ, see supra. Bava Batra 25ᵇ מתוך שמִתְחַכֵּם מתעשר because by becoming wise, he will get rich. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 33 beginning מאליו נתח׳ became wise by his own speculation.

חָרָשׁ m. (Biblical Hebrew; חָרַשׁ I) artist, artisan, carpenter, turner (faber). Devarim Rabbah section (Parashah) 2 לח׳ שהיה וכ׳ like an artist that was making an image &c.—plural חָרָשִׁים. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 65, end; section (Parashah) 70, see חֲמוֹר; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Shekalim, p. 15ᵃ.—Trsnf. scholar. Gittin 88ᵃ (reference. to II Kings XXIV, 16) חָ׳ שבשעה … כחֵרְשִׁין the scholars were named ḥarash, for when they opened argument, all were like dumb; Sanhedrin 38ᵃ; Yalkut Daniel 1066; and e.—plural as above. Chagigah 14ᵃ (reference. to Isaiah III, 3).

לַחַשׁ m. (Biblical Hebrew; preceding) whisper.—בל׳ in a low voice. Eruvin 54ᵃ היה שונה בל׳ was in the habit of studying in a low voice; (ib. 53ᵇ bottom of page גריס בלחישה). Chagigah 14ᵃ (reference. to לחש, Isaiah III, 3) זה שמוסרין לו סתרי תורה שניתנין בל׳ (see Manuscript Munich in Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. and Rashi to Isaiah l. common gender.) that is he to whom are handed over the secrets of the Law which are communicated in a low voice (compare Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 3, beginning); and e.

comments.en:
Exodus 38,23. “and at his side, Oholiov son of Achisamach ‎of the tribe of Dan, carver and designer, etc.;” Our sages in ‎‎Chagigah 14 comment on the words ‎חרש וחושב‎ by ‎explaining that the word ‎חרש‎, or ‎חרשים‎ refers to a wise student, ‎who as soon as he opens his mouth causes his teachers to become ‎even wiser when they hear his questions, whereas ‎חרשים‎ are ‎people who when they open their mouths cause others to fall ‎silent, acknowledging superior knowledge.‎
Perhaps the Talmud refers to two levels of serving G’d; the ‎first uses his intellect, i.e. the common sense G’d has endowed ‎him with to do so, whereas the second does so by contemplating ‎the enormity of the ‎אין סוף‎, the indescribable superiority of the ‎Creator, something that our common sense cannot even try to ‎comprehend. This distinction has been alluded to in Numbers ‎‎12,8 [where the subject is Miriam and Aaron having ‎compared their statures as prophets to that of Moses, ‎Ed.] When G’d explains to them that Moses’ stature of ‎prophecy enables him to ‎תמונת ה' יביט‎, “to conceptually visualize ‎the Creator as if he saw a picture of Him,” He alluded to the ‎Divine assistance Moses enjoyed when visualizing such difficult ‎concepts. He would only have been able to do so if he had first ‎abandoned and negated any attempt to comprehend G’d’s essence ‎by applying ordinary human intellect. People on that level are ‎described in the Torah as ‎חרש‎, having made themselves deaf to ‎‎“normal” ways of perceiving and comprehending phenomena ‎they see. When a person, after having been granted such ‎superhuman perceptions and insights, reverts to his day to day ‎routine, a residue of his experiences while he was on a higher ‎level remains, i.e. he is filled with ‎שפע‎, divinely transmitted ‎spiritual largesse. As a result he is able to perform the work ‎performed by embroiderers both on blue woolen fabrics, ‎תכלת‎, ‎and on purple and crimson coloured woolen fabrics, ‎ארגמן‎. ‎‎[The finished product of Oholiov’s handiwork reflected ‎that he had been divinely inspired. Ed.]‎

comments.en: The Gemara did not explain ĥakham literally, as wise man, because the word is used as part of an expression, “cunning charmer.” According to the explanation offered here, the ĥakham is the student of a charmer (Maharsha).
comments.sourceRef: Cunning [ĥakham], this is a student, etc.

sections.en: “The counselor”; this is referring to one who knows how to intercalate years and determine months, due to his expertise in the phases of the moon and the calculation of the yearly cycle. “The cunning”; this is a student who makes his rabbis wise through his questions. “Charmer [ḥarashim]”; this is referring to one so wise that when he begins speaking matters of Torah, all those listening are as though deaf [ḥershin], as they are unable to comprehend the profundity of his comments. “The skillful”; this is one who understands something new from something else he has learned. “Enchanter [laḥash]”; this is referring to one who is worthy of having words of the Torah that were given in whispers [laḥash], i.e., the secrets of the Torah, transmitted to him.

נָעַר II (Biblical Hebrew; compare עור, ערר) to shake, stir. Makhshirin I, 4 הנוֹעֵר אגודה וכ׳ he who shakes (the rain off) a bundle of vegetables. Ib. V, 7. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 26 לאיוב נָעַרְתִּי מן האשפה וכ׳ I shook Job (making him rise) from the dunghill, and concerning thee (Israel) it is written (Isaiah LII, 2), shake thyself &c.; and e.

Piël - נִיעֵר
1) to shake. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Shekalim, p. 17ᵃ נַעֲרָהּ קפלה shake it (the garment), fold it; Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 2. Bava Metzia II, 8 מצא כסות מְנַעֲרָהּ וכ׳ if one found a garment (and holds it in charge waiting for the owner to claim it), he must shake it once in thirty days. Shabbat 147ᵃ top; and from

—2) to stir. Chullin VIII, 3 נ׳ את הקדרה if he stirred (the meat in) the pot. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. I, 39ᵈ top שמא נ׳ הגוי בקדרה the gentile might have stirred the pot; and from

—3) to empty; to cause evacuation. Toharot II, 1 מְנָעֶרֶת את הקדרה she may empty (or stir) the dish. Kelim XXVIII, 2 לנָעֵר בו וכ׳ used for (lifting and) emptying the pot. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia II, 10 שהחנוני מְנָעֵר וכ׳ which the shop-keeper uses when pouring out &c. (or through which he pours for straining), see יַתִּיךְ; and e.—נ׳ את הצאן to use means by which to expedite the discharge of excrements of the flock on the spot to be manured (see דּוּר I, Piël). Tosefta Sheviit II, 20; Moʿed Katan 12ᵃ; Yerushalmi Sheviit III, 34ᶜ bottom of page Ib. השוכר … לנַעֲרָהּ he who hires a flock (for manuring) is forbidden to use means &c.; explained ib. מוליכה ממקום וכ׳ by driving it from place to place.—Part. pass. מְנוֹעָר; f. מְנוֹעֶרֶת; plural מְנוֹעָרִים, מְנוֹעָרִין: מְנוֹעָרוֹת empty, vacant. Yerushalmi Berakhot IV, 7ᵇ bottom of page (play on שִׁנְ֗עָ֗ר̇) שחם מנ׳ מן המצות וכ׳ they (the Babylonians) are vacant of (cannot perform) certain religious observances &c.; Kohelet Rabbah to XII, 7; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 37 שהיא מנ׳ וכ׳ she (Babylonia) is deprived &c. Chagigah 14ᵃ (play on נערים, Isaiah III, 4) אלו בני אדם שמנ׳ וכ׳ that means persons empty of good deeds, opposed ממולא; Yalkut Isaiah 261.—[Bava Batra 74ᵇ ור"י נוער some ed., see עוּר I.—Chullin 51ᵇ ניערה, see infra.]

Nifal - נִנְעַר
1) to be stirred up; to bestir one’s self. Bava Batra 74ᵇ וני׳ ר׳'א and R. El. was stirred up (awoke). Sotah 5ᵃ אין עפרו נ׳ his dust will not be stirred up (for resurrection). Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 1 (play on חלאה ונערה, I Chr. IV, 5) חלתה ונִנְעֲרָה מחליה וכ׳ she (Miriam) was sick, but she bestirred herself (arose) from her sickness, and the Lord restored her to youth. Yerushalmi Berakhot III, 6ᵈ top (play on מנעריו, Breishit VIII, 21) משעה שהוא נ׳ ויוצא וכ׳ from the moment the embryo bestirs itself to come out into the world; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 34; Yalkut ib. 61. Chullin 51ᵇ ננערה לעמוד וכ׳ Rashi (ed. נִיעֲרָה) if the animal made an effort to get up, although it did not succeed; and e.

—2) (of flax) to be hatcheled. Yerushalmi Shabbat II, beginning 4ᶜ (explained חוסן, ib. II, 1) פשתן שלא ננערה flax which has not yet been hatcheled.

—3) to be emptied, poured out. Yerushalmi Berakhot l. common gender. (play on שנער) ששם נִנְעֲרוּ וכ׳ for into that valley the dead of the generation of the flood were dumped; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 37; Kohelet Rabbah l. common gender.—Sanhedrin 92ᵃ קשתו נִינְעֶרֶת his bow will be empty (his sexual vitality broken).

Hifil - הִנְעִיר to stir up, to keep awake. Eruvin 53ᵇ (play on נערה &c., see אַהֲרוֹנִית) והִנְעִירָתוֹ and she kept him awake.

Hithpaël - הִתְנַעֵר to be emptied; trnsf. to be displaced. Zevachim 116ᵃ (reference. to Song of Songs IV, 16) תִּתְנַעֵר אומה … ותבא וכ׳ (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) removed be the (Roman) nation whose sacrifices are slaughtered northward (Vayikra I, 11, which is entitled only to burnt-offerings), and let the nation enter &c.

sections.en: The Gemara continues to interpret this verse: “And I will make children their princes” (Isaiah 3:4). The Gemara asks: What is the meaning of “And I will make children [ne’arim] their princes”? Rabbi Elazar said: These are people who are devoid [meno’arin] of mitzvot; such people will become the leaders of the nation.
sections.he: ״וְנָתַתִּי נְעָרִים שָׂרֵיהֶם״. מַאי ״וְנָתַתִּי נְעָרִים שָׂרֵיהֶם״? אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵלּוּ בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁמְּנוֹעָרִין מִן הַמִּצְוֹת.

השנים ובין הנער כפי מדות השכל, ומסכים לזה חכמים ז"ל (חגיגה יד, א) נערים אלו בני אדם המנוערים מן המצות, ועל זה אמר שלמה (קהלת י, טז) אי לך ארץ שמלכך נער, ואמר ותעלולים ימשלו בם, ותי"ו תעלולים נוספת ואפילו ברעהו, עד שירהבו הנער בזקן, רוצה לומר שיתגאה ויתגדל על הזקן, והנקלה על הנכבד, וזו היא הגדולה שברעות שישתנה טבע האמת ויגבר החלש ויתכבד הנקלה על הגבור ועל הנכבד ממנו, (ו) וספר שיגיע חסרון ההנהגה ביניהם עד שהם בעצמם ישתדלו להקים עליהם שוטר ומושל שיטיל מוראו עליהם כדי שיפחדו מלפניו, וכמעט מהיתרון שיכירו באחד מהם, כאלו תאמר שיהיה לו לבוש יתפשו בו קרוביו ויאמרו לו אחרי ששמלה לך ואתה לבוש בגדים חמודים, קצין תהיה לנו, והמכשלה הזאת תחת ידך, רוצה לומר העדה הרעה הזאת הנכשלת בכמה מכשולות, כמו שאמר כי כשלה יהודה, תהיה תחת ידך והנהגתך, כי כלם יכנעו למצותך, וזכר שתהיה חרפת ישראל כל כך שאפילו אדם רש ונקלה לא ירצה להיות עליהם קצין, (ז) אבל ישא וישבע ביום ההוא לאמר, שלא לבד הקצין שהוא מנוי גדול, אבל אפילו חובש בבית הסוהר לא יהיה, כי הנה אף על פי שהוא לבוש בשמלה הוא עני ודל ובביתו אין לחם ואין שמלה, וחכמת המסכן בזויה ודבריו אינם נשמעים, ולכן יהיה סוף דבריו לא תשימוני קצין עם: והנכון בעיני שהוא משיב לדבריהם שאמרו לו והמכשלה הזאת תחת ידך, והיה תשובתו לא אהיה חובש, רוצה לומר אם תהיה העדה הנכשלת הזאת תחת ידי, הנה כפי רשעתה ראוי לדון אנשיה כלם לבית האסורים, ואני איני רוצה להיות חובש שלהם, ועוד אודיעך שאם בעניני ההנהגה תכניסני הנה אמות ברעב, כי בביתי אין לחם ואין שמלה, ואם אטריד את עצמי כל היום וכל הלילה בעסקי צבור לא יהיה לי לחם לאכול ובגד ללבוש, וגם לא יהיה תפארתכם ותועלתכם שאהיה אני קצין, לפי שאתן גמולכם בראשיכם כפי רשעתכם, ולכן אומר אליכם בדרך עצה שלא תשימוני קצין עם, כי לא יהיה לטובתכם, והודיע הנביא בזה גם כן שבזמן חרבן ירושלם ירבה הדלות והעניות בעם עד אשר לא יאבה אדם שיאמרו לו שהוא עשיר ושיש לו דבר מה, יכחיש ויאמר שבביתו אין לחם ואין שמלה, וכמו שהיה במצור ירושלם בחרבן בית שני, וחכמים ז"ל דרשו (שבת קכ, א) לא אהיה חובש מחובשי בית המדר', ובביתי אין לחם ואין שמלה אין בידי לא טעם ולא משנה ולא דבר אגדה, הנה התבארו הכתובים בכל אחד מהדרכים האלה והותרה השאלה השנית:

sections.en: “And babes [ta’alulim] shall rule over them”; Rav Pappa bar Ya’akov said: Ta’alulim means foxes [ta’alei], sons of foxes. In other words, inferior people both in terms of deeds and in terms of lineage. And the prophet Isaiah’s mind was not calmed until he said to them: “The child shall behave insolently against the aged, and the base against the honorable” (Isaiah 3:5). “The child” [na’ar]; these are people who are devoid of mitzvot, who will behave insolently toward one who is as filled with mitzvot as a pomegranate. “And the base [nikleh] against the honorable [nikhbad]”; this means that one for whom major [kaved] transgressions are like minor ones [kalot] in his mind will come and behave insolently with one for whom even minor transgressions are like major ones in his mind.

en: And Rava said: Jerusalem was destroyed only because there were no more trustworthy people there, as it is stated: “Roam about the streets of Jerusalem and see, and search its plazas, if you can find a person, who acts justly, who seeks integrity, that I should forgive it” (Jeremiah 5:1). The Gemara asks: Is that so? Didn’t Rav Ketina say: Even at the time of Jerusalem’s failure, trustworthy people did not cease there, as it is stated: “For a man will grab his brother of his father’s house and say: You have a garment. Come be a chief over us and let this ruin be under your care” (Isaiah 3:6)? Things that people use to cover up like a garment, secrets, are in your hands and you know about them. Therefore, you should be a leader of the community. And that which is stated: “And let this ruin be under your care,” meaning:

Matters of Torah that people do not ascertain unless they misunderstand them are in your hands; therefore, be a chief over us. It is stated later on in that passage: “He will rise [yissa] on that day, saying, I will not be a ruler while in my house there is no bread and no garment, you shall not appoint me as chief of the people” (Isaiah 3:7). The term rise [yissa] means nothing other than an oath, as it says: “Do not raise [tissa] the name of the Lord your God in vain” (Exodus 20:17). I will not be a ruler, means: I will not be one of those who close themselves up in the study hall, as I do not regularly do so, while in my house there is no bread and no garment, for I have neither Bible nor Mishna nor Gemara in my hands. According to this explanation, there were people of faith who truthfully admitted that they did not study Torah, even during the time of the destruction of Jerusalem. The Gemara rejects this: And from what do you conclude that this admission was due to their faithfulness? Perhaps it is different in that case, as had he told them: I studied Torah, they would have said to him: Tell us what you studied. As he would not know to respond, he would have no choice other than to admit that he did not study. The Gemara rejects this: That is not difficult, as he could have at least said he learned and forgot. The Gemara asks: Therefore, what is: I will not be a ruler? It means that he is telling the truth and although he could have lied, he admits that he did not study Torah at all. The Gemara answers: This is not difficult. Here, where it was taught that they were faithful, that was with regard to matters of Torah; whereas here, where it was taught that there were no more people of faith in Jerusalem, that was with regard to matters of business.

דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵין בְּנֵי אָדָם עוֹמְדִין עֲלֵיהֶם אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְשָׁלִים בָּהֶן יֶשְׁנָן תַּחַת יָדֶיךָ, ״קָצִין תִּהְיֶה לָנוּ״. ״יִשָּׂא בַיּוֹם הַהוּא לֵאמֹר לֹא אֶהְיֶה חוֹבֵשׁ וְגוֹ׳״ — אֵין יִשָּׂא אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן שְׁבוּעָה, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר ״לֹא תִשָּׂא אֶת שֵׁם ה׳״. ״לֹא אֶהְיֶה חוֹבֵשׁ״ — לֹא אֶהְיֶה מֵחוֹבְשֵׁי עַצְמָן בְּבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ. ״וּבְבֵיתִי אֵין לֶחֶם וְאֵין שִׂמְלָה״ — שֶׁאֵין בְּיָדִי לֹא מִקְרָא וְלֹא מִשְׁנָה וְלֹא גְּמָרָא. וּמִמַּאי? דִּילְמָא שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאִי אֲמַר לְהוּ גְּמִירְנָא, אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אֵימָא לַן. הֲוָה לֵיהּ לְמֵימַר גְּמַר וּשְׁכַח, מַאי ״לֹא אֶהְיֶה חוֹבֵשׁ״? — כְּלָל! לָא קַשְׁיָא: כָּאן בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, כָּאן בְּמַשָּׂא וּמַתָּן.

sections.en: What is the meaning of the end of that verse: “And this stumbling block” (Isaiah 3:6)? Things that people cannot grasp unless they have stumbled over them, as they can be understood only with much effort, are under your hand. Although they will approach an individual with these statements, he “shall swear that day, saying: I will not be a healer, for in my house there is neither bread nor a cloak; you shall not make me ruler of a people” (Isaiah 3:7). When the verse states: “Shall swear [yissa],” yissa is none other than an expression of an oath, as it is stated: “You shall not take [tissa] the name of the Lord your God in vain” (Exodus 20:6). Therefore, the inhabitant of Jerusalem swears: “I will not be a healer [ḥovesh]” (Isaiah 3:7), which means: I was never one of those who sit [meḥovshei] in the study hall; “for in my house there is neither bread nor a cloak,” as I possess knowledge of neither the Bible, nor Mishna, nor Gemara. This shows that even at Jerusalem’s lowest spiritual ebb, its inhabitants would admit the truth and own up to their complete ignorance.

sections.en: The Gemara raises a difficulty: But perhaps it is different there, for if he had said: I have learned, they would have said to him: Tell us, and people do not lie about things that can be easily verified. The Gemara rejects this claim: If he were a liar, he would have said that he learned and forgot, thereby avoiding shame. What is the meaning of “I will not be a healer,” which seems to imply that he had learned in the past? It means: I will not be a healer at all, as I have never learned. Consequently, there were trustworthy men in Jerusalem after all.

sections.en: The Gemara raises another difficulty: Is that so? But didn’t Rava say: Jerusalem was not destroyed until trustworthy men ceased to exist in it, as it is stated: “Run to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem, and see now and know, and seek in its broad places, if you can find a man, if there is any that acts justly, that seeks truth, and I will pardon her” (Jeremiah 5:1), implying there were no trustworthy people at that time? The Gemara answers: This is not difficult:
